content.thinking: Let me get a cleaner view of the board by fetching the full JSON and parsing it.

input.command:
unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh issue list --limit 200 --state open --json number,title,labels 2>/dev/null | python3 -c "
import json, sys
issues = json.load(sys.stdin)

see_something = [(i['number'], i['title']) for i in issues if any(l['name'] == 'see-something' for l in i['labels'])]
epics = [(i['number'], i['title']) for i in issues if 'epic' in i['title'].lower() or 'Epic' in i['title']]
pipeline = [(i['number'], i['title']) for i in issues if 'Pipeline' in i['title'] or 'pipeline' in i['title']]
other = [(i['number'], i['title']) for i in issues if i not in [j for j in issues if any(l['name'] == 'see-something' for l in j['labels'])] and 'epic' not in i['title'].lower() and 'Pipeline' not in i['title'] and 'pipeline' not in i['title']]

print('=== EPICS / MEGA TASKS ===')
for n, t in epics:
    print(f'  #{n}  {t}')

print()
print('=== PIPELINE FEATURES ===')
for n, t in pipeline:
    print(f'  #{n}  {t}')

80	function buildWaves(lanePlan) {
81	  const lanes = lanePlan.lanes
82	  const ids = Object.keys(lanes)
83	  const inDeg = {}
84	  const adj = {}
85	
86	  for (const id of ids) {

88	    inDeg[id] = deps.length
89	    for (const dep of deps) {
90	      ;(adj[dep] = adj[dep] || []).push(id)
91	    }
92	  }

94	  const waves = []
95	  let queue = ids.filter(id => inDeg[id] === 0).sort()
96	
97	  while (queue.length > 0) {
98	    waves.push([...queue])
99	    const next = []
100	    for (const id of queue) {
101	      for (const child of adj[id] || []) {
102	        inDeg[child]--
103	        if (inDeg[child] === 0) next.push(child)
104	      }

126	function parseAgentJson(text, fallback) {
127	  if (!text || typeof text !== 'string') return fallback || null
128	  const cleaned = text.replace(/```[a-z]*\n?/g, '').trim()
129	  const start = cleaned.search(/[{[]/)
130	  const end = Math.max(cleaned.lastIndexOf('}'), cleaned.lastIndexOf(']'))
131	  if (start === -1 || end === -1) return fallback || null
132	  try { return JSON.parse(cleaned.slice(start, end + 1)) }
133	  catch { return fallback || null }
134	}

# DATUM — Agentic Production Line

## Commands

```
/datum go          Run from current phase through merge. Halt at gates.
/datum yolo        Skip optional gates. Hard stops still halt.
/datum <phase>     Run one phase: refine, plan, act, validate, review, closeout, etc.
/datum resume      Resume from .datum/state.json after interruption.
/datum status      Print phase, RUN_ID, lane progress, last failure.
/datum init        Bootstrap repo: hooks, linter, AGENTS.md, CURRENT_STATE.md, ROADMAP.md.
/datum rollback    Revert a merged epic. See references/rollback.md.
/datum classify    Auto-classify epic complexity (Patch/Feature/System)
/datum landscape   Generate docs/LANDSCAPE.md from filesystem analysis
/datum mermaid     Generate Mermaid diagrams — ALWAYS activates on "mermaid", "diagram", "visualize"
/datum dream       Memory consolidation — staleness audit + transcript extraction + pruning
/datum local-llm   Test local MLX inference (beta) — status check or prompt test
```

## Rule: Determinism

Orchestration is deterministic. State, transitions, routing, gates — all enforced by Python scripts. No improvisation. The LLM works within one phase. It does not decide pipeline structure or skip steps. If you are parsing history to figure out where you are, read the state file.

## Dispatcher

Execute in order before any phase work:

**0. Branch Guard** — If on `main`/`master`, auto-create a feature branch and switch. No exceptions. The branch name is descriptive, not generic (#55): slugify the brief/TICKET title into `datum/<slug>` (lowercase ASCII, hyphen-separated, ≤60 chars — `datum.slug.slugify`), de-duplicated against existing branches with a numeric suffix (`datum.slug.make_unique`). Pass the title via `datum state init --title "<title>"` (or `datum init --name "<title>"`); only when no title exists yet does it fall back to `datum/epic-{N}`. Example: "Contact Form: Server-Side Submission" → `datum/contact-form-server-side-submission`, not `datum/epic-8`.

**0.5. Self-check** — `datum doctor`. If it fails, halt.

**1. Load Config** — `.datum/config.toml`, falling back to `assets/config.toml.default`.

**2. Read State** — `datum status --json`. If no state, detect entry:

| Artifact | Entry |
|---|---|
| `docs/epics/$BRANCH/TICKET.md` | Refine |
| `docs/epics/$BRANCH/SPEC.md` (no TASKS.md) | Plan |
| `TASKS.md` + PROPERTIES.md | Act |
| PR URL | PR Comments |
| Nothing | Offer `datum init` |

Epic artifacts always live at `docs/epics/<branch>/`. Never `docs/TICKET.md`.

**2.5. Classify Complexity** — After SPEC.md is detected, run `datum classify`. Routes:

| Tier | Criteria | Pipeline |
|---|---|---|
| Patch | < 50 LOC, ≤ 1 cluster, no new public API | Express (`0x-express.md`) |
| Feature | Standard scope | Standard (full pipeline) |
| System | > 5 clusters, or new subsystem, or multi-package | Extended (units in Plan, all Properties, architect sidecar) |

User can override at `plan_human_approval` gate.

**3. Detect Language** — `datum language-detect`. Maps to `references/04-act-{lang}.md`.

**4. Resolve Tier** — `resolve_tier(phase)` returns `{phase, tier, model}` from config. See `references/model-tiers.md`.

**MANDATORY: Every subagent spawn MUST include an explicit `model:` parameter.** Read `[models.phases]` to get the tier name (e.g., `act_red = "standard"`), then resolve it via `[models]` (e.g., `standard = "claude-sonnet-4-6"`). Map to Agent parameter: `reasoning` → `model: "opus"`, `standard` → `model: "sonnet"`, `fast` → `model: "haiku"`. Never rely on the default model. The config is the authority.

**5. Dispatch Phase** — Load the reference doc, execute it, run the gate.

| Phase | Reference | Gate | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Discovery | `00-discovery.md` | — | |
| Refine | `01-refine.md` | skippable | |
| Plan | `02-plan.md` | **required** | System-tier epics include unit decomposition (step 2.5 in 02-plan.md), grouping tasks into parallelizable units of work. |
| Prior Art | `02.3-prior-art.md` | skippable | Parallel subagents search GitHub, PyPI, internal repos, and the web for existing solutions per task. Can downgrade tasks from "build" to "wrap." |
| Triage | `02.5-triage.md` | **required** | **ALWAYS runs after Prior Art.** Non-skippable, even in Express. |
| Deepen | `02.8-deepen.md` | skipped if triage routes to properties | Triage decides: deepen or skip to properties. |
| Properties | `03-properties.md` | skippable | |
| Architect | `03.5-architect.md` | blocks if ADRs missing | |
| Act | `04-act.md` | per-lane retry ladder | |
| Validate | `05-validate.md` | skippable | |
| Review | `06-review.md` | max 3 iterations | |
| PR Comments | `07-pr-comments.md` | — | |
| Closeout | `08-closeout.md` | — | |

**Sequencing rule:** After Plan gate passes, the next phase is ALWAYS Prior Art, then Triage. Never skip directly to Properties or Act. Prior Art searches for existing solutions per task (can reduce scope). Triage evaluates the plan and routes to Deepen or Properties. This is non-negotiable — skipping Triage in epic-1 caused the pipeline to miss evidence gathering.

After each phase: `datum gate <phase> [--yolo]`

| `refine_human_review` | skippable_if_complete | skipped |

## Brief Construction

The brief is the agent's entire context. Get it wrong and the contract breaks. Read `references/brief-builder.md`.

- **RED**: task entry, filtered PROPERTIES, GitNexus context, lane-tools README, stub deps. Exclude: test dir, implementation files, other lanes.
- **GREEN**: same as RED + redacted TestSignal JSON. Exclude: test source, test names, RED output.
- **REFACTOR**: everything. Full SPEC, PROPERTIES, tests, implementation, GitNexus impact.

## Artifacts

These artifacts are committed to `docs/epics/<branch>/` and archived to `.datum/runs/<RUN_ID>/`:

| Artifact | Phase | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `TICKET.md` | Input | Original request |
| `SPEC.md` | Refine | Refined requirements + Assumption Audit + Classification Metadata |
| `QUESTIONS.md` | Refine + Plan | Structured Q&A with [Answer]: tags |
| `TASKS.md` | Plan | Implementation plan (root = execution copy, epic dir = archive) |
| `PROPERTIES.md` | Properties | 11-category invariant set |
| `LANDSCAPE.md` | Discovery | Codebase architecture scaffold (project-level, not per-epic) |

## Error Recovery

- `ENVIRONMENTAL` → fix in place, same tier, counter not incremented
- `REASONING` → retry ladder: local (if enabled) → standard → reasoning → reasoning+verbose
- See `references/recovery-modes.md`

**Gemma-First Flow:** When `[local_llm] enabled = true` in config, most phases attempt local MLX inference (Gemma 4 26B) before Claude. The retry ladder: local → standard (Sonnet) → reasoning (Opus). Features:
- **Context monitoring** — checks prompt fits in 128K window before inference

# Phase: Refine

**Goal:** Transform TICKET.md into a SPEC.md that a planner can act on without asking questions.

## Inputs

- `docs/epics/<branch>/TICKET.md`
- GitNexus `context` queries on referenced symbols (if available)
- `CURRENT_STATE.md` (if present)

## Ambiguity Classification

Classify before analysis. This controls how much clarification Refine does.

| Level | Signal | Response |
|---|---|---|
| **High** | Vague or conceptual — intent unclear, architecture unspecified | Full gap analysis. Anchor every question: "I'm assuming X — is that right, or Y?" |
| **Medium** | Clear intent, detectable gaps in failure modes, NFRs, or scope | Ask about detected gaps only. Do not ask what the codebase already answers. |
| **Low** | Specific and concrete — intent, scope, failure modes all clear | Quick verify (step 1 only). Proceed to SPEC if no broken assumptions. |
| **Trivial** | Rename, tooltip, wording fix, single-line config | Trust intent. Write SPEC immediately. |

If you must assume a structural pattern, the ticket is Medium. Ask first.

Batch all questions in one message. Wait for one reply.

## Steps

### 1. Verify assumptions

For each symbol, API, or module referenced in the ticket:
- GitNexus available: `gitnexus context <symbol>` to confirm it exists
- Degraded: grep/AST to locate; record "unverified" in state
- Run impact analysis (`references/impact-analysis.md`) at d=1, d=2
- CRITICAL risk: escalate to reasoning tier for safeguard review. Record in SPEC.

Symbol does not exist → halt, ask user. Do not proceed on broken assumptions.

### 2. Identify gaps

SPEC is sufficient when it answers:
1. What user-visible behavior changes?
2. What are the failure modes and how are they handled?
3. What are the NFRs (latency, size, format)?
4. What is explicitly out of scope?
5. What are the acceptance criteria per requirement?
6. What existing behavior must remain unchanged?

Write all questions to `docs/epics/<branch>/QUESTIONS.md` using `templates/QUESTIONS.md` format:
- Add a `## Refine — YYYY-MM-DD` header
- Number questions sequentially: `### Q1: [Category] Question text?`
- Include `> context` blocks explaining why each question matters
- Leave `[Answer]:` tags empty for the human to fill
- Commit the file and wait for answers

If zero questions arise (Trivial or Low ambiguity), still create QUESTIONS.md with an empty Refine section and a note: "No clarifying questions needed — intent is clear."

In yolo mode with `skippable_if_complete` policy: ask LLM judge if the ticket answers all 6. If yes, proceed. If no, surface gaps and wait.

### 3. Resolve epic directory

```bash
BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
EPIC_DIR="docs/epics/$BRANCH"
mkdir -p "$EPIC_DIR"
```

TICKET.md should already exist at `$EPIC_DIR/TICKET.md`.

### 4. Write SPEC

Use `assets/templates/SPEC.md` as base. All sections required:

1. Summary (2-3 sentences)
2. Context
3. Requirements (numbered, each with ACs)
4. Failure modes
5. NFRs
6. Out of scope
7. Open questions (empty before gate passes)
8. Blast radius + impact analysis
9. Assumption Audit (table: #, Assumption, Justification, Status, Resolves)
10. Classification Metadata (estimated_files, estimated_loc, clusters_touched, new_public_api, dependency_additions)

Classification Metadata must be filled before the Refine gate — the classifier reads these fields to determine pipeline shape.

Every AC must be testable. If it can't become a property, it's not precise enough.

### 5. Gate

Run: `datum gate refine [--yolo]`

On pass: SPEC written to `docs/epics/<branch>/SPEC.md`, state updated.
On fail: gap list surfaced, return to step 2.

## Outputs

- `docs/epics/<branch>/TICKET.md` — original ticket, preserved
- `docs/epics/<branch>/SPEC.md` — refined requirements, ready for Plan
- `docs/epics/<branch>/QUESTIONS.md` — clarifying questions from Refine (and later Plan)

content.content:
1	# Phase: Plan
2	
3	**Goal:** Decompose docs/epics/$BRANCH/SPEC.md into a topologically-sorted, machine-readable TASKS.md where every task has a clear scope, acceptance criteria, file set, and RED note.
4	
5	## Inputs
6	
7	- `docs/epics/<branch>/SPEC.md` — refined requirements (resolve branch: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`)
8	- `docs/research/<branch>-findings.md` or `docs/adr/` — **Must be promoted from 01.5-research.md if uncertainty was high.**
9	- GitNexus `impact` on each proposed change site (if available)
10	- `CURRENT_STATE.md` (if present)
11	
12	## Steps
13	
14	### 0. Read prior failure memory
15	
16	Before decomposing tasks, read two sources of prior-epic intelligence:
17	
18	**Brief defects** (`brief_defects` arrays in prior runs' `closeout-data.json`):
19	```
20	jq -r '.brief_defects[]? | "\(.surfaced_by_stage)\t\(.missing_ac)"' .datum/runs/*/closeout-data.json 2>/dev/null || echo "(no prior closeout data)"
21	```
22	If recurring AC gaps appear (e.g., "timeout handling" or "error logging" chronically missing), write more explicit RED notes for tasks in those categories this epic.
23	
24	**ERRORS.md** (cross-session failure log):
25	```
26	cat .datum/ERRORS.md 2>/dev/null || echo "(no error history yet)"
27	```
28	Scan for entries touching files or modules relevant to this SPEC. If a prior REASONING or UNKNOWN failure targeted the same files, note the failed approach in the task decomposition so agents don't repeat it.
29	
30	Both sources are the single most actionable inputs for improving Plan quality.
31	If this is the first epic in this repo, skip this step.
32	
33	### 0.5. Surface architectural approaches before decomposing
34	
35	**Do not decompose tasks yet.** First, present 2-3 distinct architectural approaches to the human and wait for a choice.
36	
37	For each approach include:
38	- One-sentence description of the strategy
39	- Key tradeoffs (speed vs. safety, complexity vs. flexibility, etc.)
40	- Which existing modules it touches most
41	- Estimated task count and blast radius
42	
43	Example format:
44	```
45	Approach A — [name]: [1-sentence description]
46	  Tradeoffs: [what you gain / what you give up]
47	  Blast radius: [modules affected]
48	  Rough scope: ~N tasks
49	
50	Approach B — [name]: ...
51	
52	Approach C — [name]: ...
53	
54	Which approach should I decompose?
55	```
56	
57	Only proceed to step 1 after the human has chosen. If the human says "you choose" or "whatever's best", pick the simplest approach and state your choice explicitly before decomposing.
58	
59	After presenting approaches, append any implementation-level questions to `docs/epics/<branch>/QUESTIONS.md` with a `## Plan — YYYY-MM-DD` header. Use the same format as Refine questions (numbered, category-tagged, with context blocks and `[Answer]:` tags). Commit and wait for answers before decomposing.
60	
61	### 1. Impact analysis
62	
63	For each module or symbol that will change:
64	- If GitNexus available: run `gitnexus impact <symbol>` to understand blast radius; use results to group tasks by blast radius (low-impact tasks can share lanes; high-impact tasks get isolated lanes)
65	- If degraded: use heuristic file-count and LOC delta; log `risk_unknown` annotation
66	
67	### 2. Decompose into tasks
68	
69	Each task maps to one lane. A lane owns a cohesive set of files. Split tasks so:
70	- No task touches more than 5 files (guideline; exception allowed with justification)
71	- Tasks that share files go in the same lane or are sequenced with a dependency edge
72	- Tasks that introduce new public types/methods note this in the `introduces_stubs` field (RED will emit stub commits for these)
73	
74	Task shape (see `assets/schemas/task.schema.json`):
75	```json
76	{
77	  "id": "task-001",
78	  "title": "...",
79	  "description": "...",
80	  "acceptance_criteria": ["...", "..."],
81	  "files": ["Sources/...", "Tests/..."],
82	  "depends_on": [],
83	  "introduces_stubs": true,
84	  "red_note": "What the failing test should prove; which docs/PROPERTIES.md property it covers",
85	  "estimated_loc": 100
86	}
87	```
88	
89	### 2.5. Unit decomposition (System-tier only)
90	
91	**Skip this step for Patch and Feature tiers.** Only System-tier epics (as classified by `datum classify`) require unit decomposition.
92	
93	Group tasks into parallelizable units of work:
94	1. Identify independent work clusters — sets of tasks that share no files and have no behavioral dependencies
95	2. Assign each cluster a unit ID: `unit-<name>` (e.g., `unit-auth`, `unit-api`)
96	3. Map every task to exactly one unit via the `unit` field in tasks.json
97	4. Define inter-unit dependencies in the top-level `units` key:
98	
99	```json
100	{
101	  "tasks": [...],
102	  "units": {
103	    "unit-auth": { "name": "Auth Middleware", "tasks": ["task-001", "task-002"], "depends_on": [] },
104	    "unit-api": { "name": "API Endpoints", "tasks": ["task-003"], "depends_on": ["unit-auth"] }
105	  }
106	}
107	```
108	
109	**Rules:**
110	- Every task must belong to exactly one unit
111	- The unit dependency graph must be acyclic (validated by `lane_plan.py`)
112	- Tasks within a unit can run in parallel; a unit doesn't start until its dependency units complete
113	- Units that share no dependencies can be assigned to different developers
114	
115	### 3. Topological sort
116	
117	Order tasks so dependencies come first. Tasks with no dependencies can run in parallel.
118	**Goal:** Decompose docs/epics/$BRANCH/SPEC.md into a topologically-sorted, machine-readable `tasks.json` (validating against `assets/schemas/tasks.schema.json`) where every task has a clear scope, acceptance criteria, file set, and RED note. `TASKS.md` is then automatically generated from this JSON.
119	...
120	### 4. Write tasks.json
121	
122	Output the decomposed tasks as a JSON array in `tasks.json`. Ensure every field from `assets/schemas/task.schema.json` is present.
123	
124	### 5. Build lane-plan.json and TASKS.md
125	
126	Run `datum lane-plan --input tasks.json --output .datum/lane-plan.json`
127	
128	This script validates the JSON, performs the topological sort, and produces:
129	- `TASKS.md` — rendered human-readable version of the plan (root, for DATUM execution engine)
130	- `lane-plan.json` — DAG for the pipeline scheduler
131	
132	After generation, copy TASKS.md into the epic directory so it is preserved permanently:
133	
134	```bash
135	BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
136	cp TASKS.md "docs/epics/$BRANCH/TASKS.md"
137	cp tasks.json "docs/epics/$BRANCH/tasks.json"
138	```
139	
140	`TASKS.md` in the root is the live execution copy — it will be overwritten by the next epic. `docs/epics/<branch>/TASKS.md` is the permanent record.
141

# Phase: Plan

**Goal:** Decompose docs/epics/$BRANCH/SPEC.md into a topologically-sorted, machine-readable TASKS.md where every task has a clear scope, acceptance criteria, file set, and RED note.

## Inputs

- `docs/epics/<branch>/SPEC.md` — refined requirements (resolve branch: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`)
- `docs/research/<branch>-findings.md` or `docs/adr/` — **Must be promoted from 01.5-research.md if uncertainty was high.**
- GitNexus `impact` on each proposed change site (if available)
- `CURRENT_STATE.md` (if present)

## Steps

### 0. Read prior failure memory

Before decomposing tasks, read two sources of prior-epic intelligence:

**Brief defects** (`brief_defects` arrays in prior runs' `closeout-data.json`):
```
jq -r '.brief_defects[]? | "\(.surfaced_by_stage)\t\(.missing_ac)"' .datum/runs/*/closeout-data.json 2>/dev/null || echo "(no prior closeout data)"
```
If recurring AC gaps appear (e.g., "timeout handling" or "error logging" chronically missing), write more explicit RED notes for tasks in those categories this epic.

**ERRORS.md** (cross-session failure log):
```
cat .datum/ERRORS.md 2>/dev/null || echo "(no error history yet)"
```
Scan for entries touching files or modules relevant to this SPEC. If a prior REASONING or UNKNOWN failure targeted the same files, note the failed approach in the task decomposition so agents don't repeat it.

Both sources are the single most actionable inputs for improving Plan quality.
If this is the first epic in this repo, skip this step.

### 0.5. Surface architectural approaches before decomposing

**Do not decompose tasks yet.** First, present 2-3 distinct architectural approaches to the human and wait for a choice.

For each approach include:
- One-sentence description of the strategy
- Key tradeoffs (speed vs. safety, complexity vs. flexibility, etc.)
- Which existing modules it touches most
- Estimated task count and blast radius

Example format:
```
Approach A — [name]: [1-sentence description]
  Tradeoffs: [what you gain / what you give up]
  Blast radius: [modules affected]
  Rough scope: ~N tasks

Approach B — [name]: ...

Approach C — [name]: ...

Which approach should I decompose?
```

Only proceed to step 1 after the human has chosen. If the human says "you choose" or "whatever's best", pick the simplest approach and state your choice explicitly before decomposing.

After presenting approaches, append any implementation-level questions to `docs/epics/<branch>/QUESTIONS.md` with a `## Plan — YYYY-MM-DD` header. Use the same format as Refine questions (numbered, category-tagged, with context blocks and `[Answer]:` tags). Commit and wait for answers before decomposing.

### 1. Impact analysis

For each module or symbol that will change:
- If GitNexus available: run `gitnexus impact <symbol>` to understand blast radius; use results to group tasks by blast radius (low-impact tasks can share lanes; high-impact tasks get isolated lanes)
- If degraded: use heuristic file-count and LOC delta; log `risk_unknown` annotation

### 2. Decompose into tasks

Each task maps to one lane. A lane owns a cohesive set of files. Split tasks so:
- No task touches more than 5 files (guideline; exception allowed with justification)
- Tasks that share files go in the same lane or are sequenced with a dependency edge
- Tasks that introduce new public types/methods note this in the `introduces_stubs` field (RED will emit stub commits for these)

Task shape (see `assets/schemas/task.schema.json`):
```json
{
  "id": "task-001",
  "title": "...",
  "description": "...",
  "acceptance_criteria": ["...", "..."],
  "files": ["Sources/...", "Tests/..."],
  "depends_on": [],
  "introduces_stubs": true,
  "red_note": "What the failing test should prove; which docs/PROPERTIES.md property it covers",
  "estimated_loc": 100
}
```

### 2.5. Unit decomposition (System-tier only)

**Skip this step for Patch and Feature tiers.** Only System-tier epics (as classified by `datum classify`) require unit decomposition.

Group tasks into parallelizable units of work:
1. Identify independent work clusters — sets of tasks that share no files and have no behavioral dependencies
2. Assign each cluster a unit ID: `unit-<name>` (e.g., `unit-auth`, `unit-api`)
3. Map every task to exactly one unit via the `unit` field in tasks.json
4. Define inter-unit dependencies in the top-level `units` key:

```json
{
  "tasks": [...],
  "units": {
    "unit-auth": { "name": "Auth Middleware", "tasks": ["task-001", "task-002"], "depends_on": [] },
    "unit-api": { "name": "API Endpoints", "tasks": ["task-003"], "depends_on": ["unit-auth"] }
  }
}
```

**Rules:**
- Every task must belong to exactly one unit
- The unit dependency graph must be acyclic (validated by `lane_plan.py`)
- Tasks within a unit can run in parallel; a unit doesn't start until its dependency units complete
- Units that share no dependencies can be assigned to different developers

### 3. Topological sort

Order tasks so dependencies come first. Tasks with no dependencies can run in parallel.
**Goal:** Decompose docs/epics/$BRANCH/SPEC.md into a topologically-sorted, machine-readable `tasks.json` (validating against `assets/schemas/tasks.schema.json`) where every task has a clear scope, acceptance criteria, file set, and RED note. `TASKS.md` is then automatically generated from this JSON.
...
### 4. Write tasks.json

Output the decomposed tasks as a JSON array in `tasks.json`. Ensure every field from `assets/schemas/task.schema.json` is present.

### 5. Build lane-plan.json and TASKS.md

Run `datum lane-plan --input tasks.json --output .datum/lane-plan.json`

This script validates the JSON, performs the topological sort, and produces:
- `TASKS.md` — rendered human-readable version of the plan (root, for DATUM execution engine)
- `lane-plan.json` — DAG for the pipeline scheduler

After generation, copy TASKS.md into the epic directory so it is preserved permanently:

```bash
BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
cp TASKS.md "docs/epics/$BRANCH/TASKS.md"
cp tasks.json "docs/epics/$BRANCH/tasks.json"
```

`TASKS.md` in the root is the live execution copy — it will be overwritten by the next epic. `docs/epics/<branch>/TASKS.md` is the permanent record.

### 6. Gate

Before running the gate, the agent MUST complete the `## Assumption Audit` section in docs/epics/<branch>/SPEC.md:
- List at least 3 assumptions baked into the SPEC
- For each: state the assumption, justify it, and mark Status as `confirmed` or `guess`
- For `guess` entries: add `Resolves: Q<N>` pointing to an answered question in QUESTIONS.md
- If the Refine phase generated zero questions, note this — the gate will emit a warning

Run `datum gate plan [--yolo]`

Validates:
1. Every task has `acceptance_criteria`, `files`, `red_note`
2. DAG is acyclic and all dependency IDs resolve
3. No task is missing a `depends_on` entry when its `files` overlap with another task
4. If `plan_human_approval = required`: presents `tasks.json` and `TASKS.md` to user for approval

On pass: update state.
On fail: surface the validation errors and rework.

## Outputs

| File | Location | Purpose |
|------|----------|---------|
| `tasks.json` | repo root + `docs/epics/<branch>/` | Structured task list |
| `TASKS.md` | repo root (execution) + `docs/epics/<branch>/` (archive) | Rendered implementation plan |
| `lane-plan.json` | `.datum/` | DAG for pipeline scheduler |
| `docs/epics/<branch>/QUESTIONS.md` | `docs/epics/<branch>/` | Plan-section questions appended |


## Failure modes

- TASKS.md not topo-sorted → `datum lane-plan --validate` exits 1; skill rewrites
- TASKS.md missing RED note per task → gate exits 1; skill rewrites
- Circular dependency detected → halt, surface the cycle, ask user how to resolve

content.thinking:
The user is asking a great question about parallelism in the datum-tdd-act workflow. Let me think about this carefully.

Looking at the current workflow structure:

1. **Within a wave** — tasks run in parallel (good, already happening)
2. **Between waves** — Wave 2 can't start until Wave 1 finishes, Wave 3 can't start until Wave 2 finishes (this is the bottleneck)

But the user is asking: are there cases where we're waiting for something unrelated to finish before starting something that could run independently?

Looking at the dependency graph in our TASKS.md:
```
task-003 (DuckDB backup) --> task-006 (schema migration)
task-002 (PipelineCoordinator) --> task-010 (Recording Notice)
task-007 (Localization) --> task-011 (Onboarding)
task-007 (Localization) --> task-012 (Accessibility)
task-006 (schema migration) --> task-013 (Crash resilience)
task-006 (schema migration) --> task-014 (Uninstall/cleanup)
```

So Wave 1 has 8 tasks running in parallel, and Wave 2 contains 4 tasks that depend on Wave 1 completions.

Looking at the actual parallelism opportunities, task-010 only depends on task-002, so it could theoretically start as soon as task-002 finishes rather than waiting for the full Wave 1 to complete. But in practice, grouping it with Wave 2 alongside task-006, task-011, and task-012 still achieves parallelism since those other tasks are also finishing around the same time. Let me trace through the dependencies more carefully to see if there's any actual slack in the schedule. and task-014 can both start once task-006 finishes. The real issue is that the wave-based approach creates a synchronization barrier — task-010 gets blocked waiting for the entire first wave to complete, even though it only depends on task-002. A better approach would be using a pipeline model instead, where each task advances independently as soon as its dependencies are satisfied, eliminating those artificial delays between waves.

Within the RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle itself, there's already some parallelization happening with the skeptic panel running its three lenses concurrently, and the refactor-check stays sequential by design. The biggest win would be switching away from the wave barrier entirely to a true DAG-aware execution model.

Looking at how the workflow currently batches tasks into waves and waits for all of them to complete before moving to the next level, this creates unnecessary idle time when downstream tasks only depend on a subset of the current wave. A pipeline-based approach would let each task start the moment its specific dependencies finish, rather than waiting for the entire wave to complete.

I'm also noticing there are other parallelism opportunities being missed. The RED reflection and signal extraction phases run sequentially but they're actually independent — the reflection agent evaluates test quality while the signal extraction agent pulls failure messages, so these could run concurrently. Similarly, the docs phase is currently a single agent handling all 14 tasks, which might benefit from parallelization as well.

The batch grouping is another constraint worth examining — we're capping at 5 lanes per batch even though we have 16 agent slots available, so we could likely run 8 or more lanes simultaneously in the first wave without hitting limits. The real win would be implementing true DAG scheduling so tasks start the moment their dependencies finish rather than waiting for entire waves to complete.

content.text:
Yes, two real opportunities:

**1. Wave barrier is unnecessarily conservative (biggest win)**

The workflow uses Kahn's BFS to group tasks into waves, then `parallel()` with a full barrier between waves. That means every task in Wave N+1 waits for the *slowest* task in Wave N — even if its only dependency finished 20 minutes ago.

In our run: task-010 (Recording Notice) only depends on task-002 (PipelineCoordinator). But it had to wait for task-007 (Localization, ~250 LOC) to finish before it could start — even though those two tasks share zero files and have no relationship. That's dead wall-clock time.

The fix is switching from `waves → parallel()` to `pipeline()` per task, starting each lane the moment its own deps land commits — not when the whole wave clears.

**2. Reflection + test signal are sequential within each lane but don't depend on each other**

After RED commits, the lane runs:
1. `reflect` agent (judges test quality)
2. `signal` agent (extracts failure messages for GREEN)

These are independent. They could run as `parallel([reflect, signal])`, saving ~30-60s per lane × 14 lanes.

**Not a problem:**
- The 3-lens skeptic panel is already parallel ✓
- The haiku refactor-check before sonnet is intentionally sequential ✓

   - **datum-tdd-act Workflow**: RED→GREEN→REFACTOR per lane with gate enforcement, uses git worktrees for isolation
   - **Wave-based parallelism**: BFS topological sort groups tasks into waves; all of wave N must finish before wave N+1 starts (barrier model)
   - **Workflow resume**: Caches agent() calls by (prompt, opts) hash; different worktree paths = cache miss = redo all work
   - **Git worktrees**: Each lane runs in an isolated worktree on branch `datum/beta-ga-readiness--task-XXX`
   - **System tier**: Epic classification requiring unit decomposition, 10 clusters, 45-60 files, 2500-3500 LOC
   - **TDD gate enforcement**: RED must fail before GREEN can start; verify-stage checks enforce this

# TICKET: BETA / GA Readiness

**Branch:** datum/beta-ga-readiness  
**Date:** 2026-06-13  
**Source issues:** #68, #69, #71, #72, #73, #116, #117, #119, #120, #121, #122, #123, #124, #125

---

## Request

Close the remaining BETA and GA-readiness gaps before the public launch of THE RECORD. These are the items on the board that sit between "working software" and "shippable product."

---

## Scope

### Beta (pre-launch polish)

- **#68** — Recording Notice UI: per-session disclosure modal before first audio capture (legal / App Store requirement).
- **#69** — DuckDB auto-backup on quit: copy `.duckdb` → `.duckdb.bak` after WAV flush on `applicationWillTerminate`.
- **#71** — Entitlements review: audit and remove non-essential entitlements before public distribution.
- **#72** — SearchVM ↔ LibraryVM wiring: stale search results after library reloads (active bug, users see old results).
- **#73** — PipelineCoordinator cleanup: `BroadsheetAppStatePipeline` stuck in `.pending` state after stop.

### GA (launch-blocking)

- **#116** — Crash resilience: graceful recovery when WhisperKit/MLX crashes mid-transcription (no data loss, re-queue).
- **#117** — Onboarding: guided first-run permission flow (mic, screen, calendar) + first-recording tutorial overlay.
- **#119** — Error reporting: opt-in crash and diagnostics telemetry (no PII, local-first story preserved).
- **#120** — Accessibility audit: VoiceOver labels, keyboard navigation, Dynamic Type support.
- **#121** — Localization infrastructure: strings extraction + base `.lproj` structure (English only for v1; infra for v2 translations).
- **#122** — Data migration: DuckDB schema versioning + migration runner (so upgrades don't corrupt existing recordings).
- **#123** — Uninstall / data cleanup: "Delete all data" option in Settings + uninstall documentation.
- **#124** — Storage guard: disk space warnings, max-duration cap, old-recording cleanup policy.
- **#125** — Keychain hardening: audit `kSecAttr` settings, access groups, token storage patterns.

### Explicitly out of scope (separate epics)

- #70 (App icon / screenshots) — design asset, not code
- #74 (StoreKit IAP) — separate billing epic
- #75 (App Store compliance) — depends on #74
- #76 (HIPAA / SOC 2) — enterprise readiness, separate track
- #77 (WER/DER metrics) — QA tooling, separate track
- #118 (Sparkle auto-update) — delivery infrastructure, separate track

---

## Success Criteria

1. All 14 in-scope issues closed.
2. App passes a first-run flow on a clean Mac without crashing or surfacing an uncaught error.
3. `swift build -strict-concurrency=complete` emits no new warnings.
4. No regressions in existing test suite.
5. Schema migration runner boots successfully on a DuckDB from the previous build.

No clarifying questions needed — all 15 bugs are specific, have known file locations, and have clear fixes described in the TICKET.md and GitHub issues.

# DATUM — Agentic Production Line

## Commands

```
/datum go          Run from current phase through merge. Halt at gates.
/datum yolo        Skip optional gates. Hard stops still halt.
/datum <phase>     Run one phase: refine, plan, act, validate, review, closeout, etc.
/datum resume      Resume from .datum/state.json after interruption.
/datum status      Print phase, RUN_ID, lane progress, last failure.
/datum init        Bootstrap repo: hooks, linter, AGENTS.md, CURRENT_STATE.md, ROADMAP.md.
/datum rollback    Revert a merged epic. See references/rollback.md.
/datum classify    Auto-classify epic complexity (Patch/Feature/System)
/datum landscape   Generate docs/LANDSCAPE.md from filesystem analysis
/datum mermaid     Generate Mermaid diagrams — ALWAYS activates on "mermaid", "diagram", "visualize"
/datum dream       Memory consolidation — staleness audit + transcript extraction + pruning
/datum local-llm   Test local MLX inference (beta) — status check or prompt test
```

## Rule: Determinism

Orchestration is deterministic. State, transitions, routing, gates — all enforced by Python scripts. No improvisation. The LLM works within one phase. It does not decide pipeline structure or skip steps. If you are parsing history to figure out where you are, read the state file.

## Dispatcher

Execute in order before any phase work:

**0. Branch Guard** — If on `main`/`master`, auto-create a feature branch and switch. No exceptions. The branch name is descriptive, not generic (#55): slugify the brief/TICKET title into `datum/<slug>` (lowercase ASCII, hyphen-separated, ≤60 chars — `datum.slug.slugify`), de-duplicated against existing branches with a numeric suffix (`datum.slug.make_unique`). Pass the title via `datum state init --title "<title>"` (or `datum init --name "<title>"`); only when no title exists yet does it fall back to `datum/epic-{N}`. Example: "Contact Form: Server-Side Submission" → `datum/contact-form-server-side-submission`, not `datum/epic-8`.

**0.5. Self-check** — `datum doctor`. If it fails, halt.

**1. Load Config** — `.datum/config.toml`, falling back to `assets/config.toml.default`.

**2. Read State** — `datum status --json`. If no state, detect entry:

| Artifact | Entry |
|---|---|
| `docs/epics/$BRANCH/TICKET.md` | Refine |
| `docs/epics/$BRANCH/SPEC.md` (no TASKS.md) | Plan |
| `TASKS.md` + PROPERTIES.md | Act |
| PR URL | PR Comments |
| Nothing | Offer `datum init` |

Epic artifacts always live at `docs/epics/<branch>/`. Never `docs/TICKET.md`.

**2.5. Classify Complexity** — After SPEC.md is detected, run `datum classify`. Routes:

| Tier | Criteria | Pipeline |
|---|---|---|
| Patch | < 50 LOC, ≤ 1 cluster, no new public API | Express (`0x-express.md`) |
| Feature | Standard scope | Standard (full pipeline) |
| System | > 5 clusters, or new subsystem, or multi-package | Extended (units in Plan, all Properties, architect sidecar) |

User can override at `plan_human_approval` gate.

**3. Detect Language** — `datum language-detect`. Maps to `references/04-act-{lang}.md`.

**4. Resolve Tier** — `resolve_tier(phase)` returns `{phase, tier, model}` from config. See `references/model-tiers.md`.

**MANDATORY: Every subagent spawn MUST include an explicit `model:` parameter.** Read `[models.phases]` to get the tier name (e.g., `act_red = "standard"`), then resolve it via `[models]` (e.g., `standard = "claude-sonnet-4-6"`). Map to Agent parameter: `reasoning` → `model: "opus"`, `standard` → `model: "sonnet"`, `fast` → `model: "haiku"`. Never rely on the default model. The config is the authority.

**5. Dispatch Phase** — Load the reference doc, execute it, run the gate.

| Phase | Reference | Gate | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Discovery | `00-discovery.md` | — | |
| Refine | `01-refine.md` | skippable | |
| Plan | `02-plan.md` | **required** | System-tier epics include unit decomposition (step 2.5 in 02-plan.md), grouping tasks into parallelizable units of work. |
| Prior Art | `02.3-prior-art.md` | skippable | Parallel subagents search GitHub, PyPI, internal repos, and the web for existing solutions per task. Can downgrade tasks from "build" to "wrap." |
| Triage | `02.5-triage.md` | **required** | **ALWAYS runs after Prior Art.** Non-skippable, even in Express. |
| Deepen | `02.8-deepen.md` | skipped if triage routes to properties | Triage decides: deepen or skip to properties. |
| Properties | `03-properties.md` | skippable | |
| Architect | `03.5-architect.md` | blocks if ADRs missing | |
| Act | `04-act.md` | per-lane retry ladder | |
| Validate | `05-validate.md` | skippable | |
| Review | `06-review.md` | max 3 iterations | |
| PR Comments | `07-pr-comments.md` | — | |
| Closeout | `08-closeout.md` | — | |

**Sequencing rule:** After Plan gate passes, the next phase is ALWAYS Prior Art, then Triage. Never skip directly to Properties or Act. Prior Art searches for existing solutions per task (can reduce scope). Triage evaluates the plan and routes to Deepen or Properties. This is non-negotiable — skipping Triage in epic-1 caused the pipeline to miss evidence gathering.

After each phase: `datum gate <phase> [--yolo]`

For Act, also load: `agent-contracts.md`, `brief-builder.md`, `04-act-red-brief.md`, `04-act-green-brief.md`, `04-act-refactor-brief.md`, `04-act-adversarial-brief.md`, `04-act-skeleton-preflight.md`, `pipeline-dispatch.md`, `proof-of-work.md`, `spec-drift.md`, `quality-profiles.md`, language override, `gitnexus-playbook.md` (if available).

## Gates

| Gate | Policy | yolo? |
|---|---|---|
| `refine_human_review` | skippable_if_complete | skipped |
| `plan_human_approval` | **required** | **halts** |
| `triage_human_approval` | **required** | **halts** |
| `properties_human_review` | skippable_if_complete | skipped |
| `validate_human_review` | skippable_if_complete | skipped |
| `merge_human_approval` | **required** | **halts** |

> Plan gate also checks: `## Assumption Audit` in SPEC.md (fails if missing or has unresolved guesses). Emits warning if Refine generated zero questions in QUESTIONS.md.

Hard stops never bypass: `tests_red_after_3x_retry`, `hook_blocked_write`, `merge_conflict`, `git_push_rejected`, `schema_validation_failed`, `test_ratchet_violation`, `lane_tool_sandbox_violation`, `external_dependency_install_proposed`.

## Brief Construction

The brief is the agent's entire context. Get it wrong and the contract breaks. Read `references/brief-builder.md`.

- **RED**: task entry, filtered PROPERTIES, GitNexus context, lane-tools README, stub deps. Exclude: test dir, implementation files, other lanes.
- **GREEN**: same as RED + redacted TestSignal JSON. Exclude: test source, test names, RED output.
- **REFACTOR**: everything. Full SPEC, PROPERTIES, tests, implementation, GitNexus impact.

## Artifacts

These artifacts are committed to `docs/epics/<branch>/` and archived to `.datum/runs/<RUN_ID>/`:

| Artifact | Phase | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `TICKET.md` | Input | Original request |
| `SPEC.md` | Refine | Refined requirements + Assumption Audit + Classification Metadata |
| `QUESTIONS.md` | Refine + Plan | Structured Q&A with [Answer]: tags |
| `TASKS.md` | Plan | Implementation plan (root = execution copy, epic dir = archive) |
| `PROPERTIES.md` | Properties | 11-category invariant set |
| `LANDSCAPE.md` | Discovery | Codebase architecture scaffold (project-level, not per-epic) |

## Error Recovery

- `ENVIRONMENTAL` → fix in place, same tier, counter not incremented
- `REASONING` → retry ladder: local (if enabled) → standard → reasoning → reasoning+verbose
- See `references/recovery-modes.md`

**Gemma-First Flow:** When `[local_llm] enabled = true` in config, most phases attempt local MLX inference (Gemma 4 26B) before Claude. The retry ladder: local → standard (Sonnet) → reasoning (Opus). Features:
- **Context monitoring** — checks prompt fits in 128K window before inference
- **Repetition detection** — aborts and escalates if output loops (n-gram detection)
- **Grammar-constrained output** — `datum.local_llm.structured(prompt, Schema)` via outlines forces valid JSON
- **Escalation signal** — model outputs `ESCALATE` or pipeline detects failure → bumps to Claude
- **Metrics** — `datum local-llm --stats` tracks calls, tokens, escalation rate, estimated savings
- Phases routed locally: triage, skeleton, RED, GREEN, REFACTOR, validate, sidecars, closeout collectors

**Self-healing:** On any unexpected error (script crash, missing asset, schema failure on DATUM-generated artifacts), run `datum bugfile <module> "<description>" --trace "<traceback>"` or call `datum.report_bug.report_bug(module, error, context)` from Python. Auto-files a deduplicated GitHub issue with `datum-bug` label. See `AGENTS.md` for the full policy.

## Resume

`datum resume` reads state and continues where it stopped. Completed phases are not re-run. ACT lanes with `in_progress` are re-queued. See `references/recovery-modes.md`.

## Session End

On "session end" or "wrapping up" during a DATUM run, write a handoff to memory:

```
Run ID / Phase / Branch / Lane summary / Decisions / Next action
```

Write to: `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/datum-session-<timestamp>.md`

## Mermaid Diagrams

**Trigger:** Always activates on "mermaid", "diagram", "visualize", "draw the flow", "sequence diagram", "architecture diagram", or `/datum mermaid`.

Built-in diagram and design-doc capability. References and templates are part of the datum package:

| Resource | Use for |
|----------|---------|
| `references/mermaid-diagram-guide.md` | Syntax reference for all diagram types |
| `references/sequence-diagrams.md` | Sequence diagram patterns |
| `references/activity-diagrams.md` | Activity/flowchart patterns |
| `references/architecture-diagrams.md` | C4 and architecture patterns |
| `references/deployment-diagrams.md` | Infrastructure diagrams |
| `references/diagram-legibility.md` | High-contrast styling rules |
| `references/unicode-symbols.md` | Semantic unicode for diagram labels |
| `references/troubleshooting.md` | Mermaid syntax error fixes |
| `references/resilient-workflow.md` | Validate-before-embed workflow |

**Templates:** `templates/system-design-template.md`, `templates/architecture-design-template.md`, `templates/api-design-template.md`, `templates/feature-design-template.md`, `templates/database-design-template.md`

**Scripts:** `scripts/resilient_diagram.py` (validate), `scripts/mermaid_to_image.py` (render PNG), `scripts/extract_mermaid.py` (extract from markdown)

**Rules:**
1. NEVER embed a diagram without validating it first via `datum mermaid validate`
2. ALWAYS use high-contrast styling and unicode semantic symbols
3. PREFER design templates from `templates/` when creating design documents

## Cross-Tool

SKILL.md is tool-agnostic. Subagent primitives are in `assets/config.toml.default` under `[tools]`. Model tiers resolve per-tool via `[models]`. See `references/model-tiers.md`.

- NEVER ignore HIGH or CRITICAL risk warnings from impact analysis.
- NEVER rename symbols with find-and-replace — use `gitnexus_rename` which understands the call graph.

# No Embedded Languages ## What This Is A mandatory rule preventing inline embedding of non-Swift languages in Swift source files. All foreign-language content must live in dedicated files so it can be linted, reviewed, and tested as its own source. ## When to Apply Every time you write or edit Swift code that would contain non-Swift content inline — SQL, JSON schemas, LLM prompts, shell commands, HTML, regex, or any other language embedded as string literals. ## The Rule **Never embed non-Swift languages as inline string literals in Swift source.** Extract them into dedicated files and reference them from Swift. ### What counts as an embedded language | Language | Example | Extract to | |----------|---------|-----------| | SQL | `"SELECT ... FROM ..."` | `*SQL.swift` enum with static funcs | | LLM prompts | `"You are a ..."` | `*Prompts.swift` enum with static funcs | | JSON schemas/templates | `{"key": "..."}` | `*Prompts.swift` or `*Schema.swift` | | JSON-RPC / wire protocols | `["jsonrpc": "2.0", ...]` | `*Protocol.swift` enum | | Shell commands | `"/bin/sh -c ..."` | `*Commands.swift` enum | | HTML templates | `"
...
"` | `*Templates.swift` enum | | Regex patterns | `"^[a-z]+\\d{3}$"` | `*Patterns.swift` enum | ### Naming convention The extracted file lives next to the consumer and uses a suffix that describes the embedded language: ``` Infrastructure/Storage/DuckDBSQL.swift — SQL for DuckDBStorageActor Infrastructure/Summarization/SummarizationPrompts.swift — LLM prompts Infrastructure/MCP/MCPProtocol.swift — JSON-RPC wire format ``` ### Pattern Use a caseless `enum` with static functions or properties: ```swift enum DuckDBSQL { static let createRecordings = "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ..." static func selectRecording(id: String) -> String { ... } } ``` The consumer calls `DuckDBSQL.selectRecording(id: id)` — no inline SQL. ## Why 1. **Lintable** — SQL, JSON, and prompts in their own files can have dedicated lint rules, line length checks, and format validation without fighting Swift's string escaping. 2. **Reviewable** — PRs that change SQL or prompts show up as changes to a clearly-named file, not buried inside business logic. 3. **Testable** — extracted prompts and queries can be unit tested for structure, required fields, and format without instantiating the consumer. 4. **Discoverable** — `grep` for all SQL → look in `*SQL.swift`. Grep for all prompts → look in `*Prompts.swift`. No hunting through actor files. 5. **Drift-resistant** — when a DTO struct changes shape, the co-located prompt file is an obvious place to update. Inline strings get forgotten. ## Exceptions - **Trivial single-value strings** that happen to be another language but are under 80 characters and non-reusable (e.g. `"DELETE FROM x WHERE id = ?"`) may stay inline if extracting would add ceremony without value. - **Test fixtures** — test files may contain inline examples for readability. ## Existing extractions | File | Contains | Consumer | |------|----------|----------| | `DuckDBSQL.swift` | All DuckDB SQL | `DuckDBStorageActor` | | `SummarizationPrompts.swift` | LLM prompt + JSON schema | `MLXSummarizationPlugin` | | `MCPProtocol.swift` | JSON-RPC request builder | `GenericMCPProvider` |

#68 [OPEN] beta: Recording Notice UI — per-session disclosure before first capture
## User Story

**As a** user about to record a meeting for the first time,
**I want** THE RECORD to show me a clear disclosure that recording is about to begin,
**so that** I can inform other participants and comply with recording consent laws in my jurisdiction.

## Context

Recording consent laws

#69 [OPEN] beta: DuckDB auto-backup on quit — WAV checkpoint then copy .duckdb to .duckdb.bak
## User Story

**As a** user whose app crashes mid-meeting,
**I want** THE RECORD to automatically back up my database on quit so I never lose recordings or transcripts,
**so that** my data survives crashes, forced quits, and unexpected shutdowns.

## Context

DuckDB is the single store for all reco
---
#71 [OPEN] beta: Entitlements review — remove non-essential entitlements before public distribution

# eedom Container Build & Test

Everything needed to build and run eedom's test containers without guessing.

## The uv + Docker Problem

`uv` uses tokio async runtime which registers Unix signal handlers via `socketpair()`.
Docker's default seccomp profile blocks this syscall, causing a panic. This is NOT an
eedom bug — it is a uv + Docker seccomp interaction.

## Deterministic Build Commands

### Docker (x86 Linux — CI and sambou@192.168.0.210)

```bash
# One-time builder setup (already done on 192.168.0.210)
docker buildx create --name eedom-builder --driver docker-container \
  --buildkitd-flags '--allow-insecure-entitlement security.insecure' --use

# Build
docker buildx build --allow security.insecure --load \
  --platform linux/amd64 -f Dockerfile.test -t eedom-test:amd64 .

# Run tests
docker run --rm --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --entrypoint "" \
  eedom-test:amd64 /opt/test-venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -v
```

### Podman (macOS arm64 — local dev)

```bash
# Build
podman build --security-opt apparmor=unconfined \
  --platform linux/amd64 -f Dockerfile.test -t eedom-test:amd64 .

# Run tests
podman run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --security-opt apparmor=unconfined \
  --entrypoint "" eedom-test:amd64 /opt/test-venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -v
```

### Or just

```bash
make test
```

The Makefile detects docker vs podman and applies the right flags automatically.

## Dockerfile.test Rules

1. Line 1 MUST be `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1` — enables BuildKit RUN flags
2. Every `RUN` calling `uv` MUST have `--security=insecure` prefix
3. `RUN apt-get` and `RUN groupadd` do NOT need `--security=insecure`
4. Pin uv image by sha256 digest — never use `:latest` (supply chain risk)
5. Set `UV_NO_PROGRESS=1` in ENV block

## Container ENTRYPOINT is `["uv", "run"]`

This causes the tokio panic at runtime. ALWAYS override it:
- Pass `--entrypoint ""` on the run command
- Use `/opt/test-venv/bin/python` — NOT `python3` (system python, outside venv)

## Key Paths Inside Container

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `/opt/test-venv/bin/python` | USE THIS for pytest |
| `/opt/test-venv/` | Virtual environment |
| `/workspace/` | Repo mount point |
| `/usr/local/bin/uv` | uv binary |

## Error to Fix Lookup Table

| Error | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| `AppArmor is not initialized correctly` | Add `--security-opt apparmor=unconfined` to podman build |
| `security.insecure is not allowed` | Create docker buildx builder with `--allow-insecure-entitlement security.insecure` |
| `failed to create UnixStream: Permission denied` | Override entrypoint with `--entrypoint ""` OR add `--security=insecure` to Dockerfile RUN |
| `No module named pytest` | Use `/opt/test-venv/bin/python` not `python3` |
| `COPY --from no stage found` | Digest does not resolve cross-platform — verify on target arch |
| `No module named 'tests'` | Add empty `tests/__init__.py` |

## x86 Test Host

```
sambou@192.168.0.210 — Debian 13, Docker 26.1.5, x86_64
Builder: eedom-builder (insecure entitlements enabled)
```

## Before Editing ANY Container Config

1. Read THIS skill first
2. Use context7 MCP for Docker/Podman/uv docs if uncertain
3. Test on x86 host via SSH — not locally on macOS
4. `make test` is the source of truth

# eedom — working facts

**What/where**: org's deterministic code reviewer (pure AST + sqlite CodeGraph + scanners: blast-radius, complexity, gitleaks, semgrep/opengrep). Repo: `/Volumes/Extra/repos/gitrdunhq/eedom` (github.com/gitrdunhq/eedom). ~2,130 unit tests, SLSA L3 CI, release-please.

**Merge mechanics (learned the hard way, see episodic [[eedom-rebase-only-pr-saga]])**:
- REBASE-ONLY: `allow_merge_commit=false`, `allow_squash_merge=false`. Branch protection requires the `Gate` status check AND up-to-date branch.
- Rebase-merge REWRITES SHAs → a branch's base commit never lands on main as-is. Never base follow-up branches on a branch awaiting rebase-merge.
- Serial merges invalidate the next PR's base (BEHIND) → `gh pr update-branch --rebase` (never plain update — a merge commit makes the PR un-rebase-merge-able: "This branch can't be rebased").
- PRs with merge conflicts get NO CI (GitHub can't build the test merge → pull_request workflows never fire → "Gate is expected" forever).
- Landing: `gh pr merge N --rebase --admin` (admin needed; no review approvals configured).

**Test conventions**: repo policy is container-only (`make test`); host runs need `EEDOM_ALLOW_HOST_TESTS=1 uv run pytest`. 3 `test_dockerfile.py` integration failures on host = stale local container image, pre-existing.

**Binary skew**: `~/.local/bin/eedom` is v0.2.8 vs repo 0.2.24+ — the datum-local gate runs the OLD binary until reinstalled. v0.2.8 lacks: CLI path scoping, non-empty messages (#390), XDG graph-db location (#391), venv detection (#388), `eedom schema` (#389).

**Config**: `.eagle-eyed-dom.yaml` in the reviewed repo — scanner enable/disable, thresholds, and (post-#393) `plugins.semgrep.extra_config_dirs` + `exclude_rules`. `.eedomignore` for path exclusions. Semgrep local rules also hardcoded to `<repo>/policies/semgrep/`.

**Known open issues**: #396 fails OPEN when opengrep aborts (broken symlink → "verdict: clear"); #395 project-board PAT dead (workflows disabled 2026-06-11, Sam must rotate `GITRDUNHQ_PROJECT_BOT`).

**Community rules quality**: two path rules = 679 FPs / 0 TPs on datum (excluded). Datum's tuned config: 13 excluded rules, 14 nosemgrep sites, proof run = 2 intentional findings.

# eedom container scan - run from any repo
dom() {
  local repo="${1:-.}"
  local format="${2:-json}"
  local abs_repo=$(cd "$repo" && pwd)
  local name=$(basename "$abs_repo")
  mkdir -p "$abs_repo/.temp"
  podman run --rm \
    --platform linux/amd64 \
    -v "$abs_repo:/workspace:ro" \
    -v "$abs_repo/.temp:/workspace/.temp" \
    eedom:latest \
    review --repo-path /workspace --all --format "$format" \
    --output "/workspace/.temp/eedom-review.$format"
  echo "Results: $abs_repo/.temp/eedom-review.$format"
}

Base directory for this skill: /Users/samfakhreddine/.claude/skills/eedom-container

# eedom Container Build & Test

Everything needed to build and run eedom's test containers without guessing.

## The uv + Docker Problem

`uv` uses tokio async runtime which registers Unix signal handlers via `socketpair()`.
Docker's default seccomp profile blocks this syscall, causing a panic. This is NOT an
eedom bug — it is a uv + Docker seccomp interaction.

## Deterministic Build Commands

### Docker (x86 Linux — CI and sambou@192.168.0.210)

```bash
# One-time builder setup (already done on 192.168.0.210)
docker buildx create --name eedom-builder --driver docker-container \
  --buildkitd-flags '--allow-insecure-entitlement security.insecure' --use

# Build
docker buildx build --allow security.insecure --load \
  --platform linux/amd64 -f Dockerfile.test -t eedom-test:amd64 .

# Run tests
docker run --rm --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --entrypoint "" \
  eedom-test:amd64 /opt/test-venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -v
```

### Podman (macOS arm64 — local dev)

```bash
# Build
podman build --security-opt apparmor=unconfined \
  --platform linux/amd64 -f Dockerfile.test -t eedom-test:amd64 .

# Run tests
podman run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --security-opt apparmor=unconfined \
  --entrypoint "" eedom-test:amd64 /opt/test-venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -v
```

### Or just

```bash
make test
```

The Makefile detects docker vs podman and applies the right flags automatically.

## Dockerfile.test Rules

1. Line 1 MUST be `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1` — enables BuildKit RUN flags
2. Every `RUN` calling `uv` MUST have `--security=insecure` prefix
3. `RUN apt-get` and `RUN groupadd` do NOT need `--security=insecure`
4. Pin uv image by sha256 digest — never use `:latest` (supply chain risk)
5. Set `UV_NO_PROGRESS=1` in ENV block

## Container ENTRYPOINT is `["uv", "run"]`

This causes the tokio panic at runtime. ALWAYS override it:
- Pass `--entrypoint ""` on the run command
- Use `/opt/test-venv/bin/python` — NOT `python3` (system python, outside venv)

## Key Paths Inside Container

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `/opt/test-venv/bin/python` | USE THIS for pytest |
| `/opt/test-venv/` | Virtual environment |
| `/workspace/` | Repo mount point |
| `/usr/local/bin/uv` | uv binary |

## Error to Fix Lookup Table

| Error | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| `AppArmor is not initialized correctly` | Add `--security-opt apparmor=unconfined` to podman build |
| `security.insecure is not allowed` | Create docker buildx builder with `--allow-insecure-entitlement security.insecure` |
| `failed to create UnixStream: Permission denied` | Override entrypoint with `--entrypoint ""` OR add `--security=insecure` to Dockerfile RUN |
| `No module named pytest` | Use `/opt/test-venv/bin/python` not `python3` |
| `COPY --from no stage found` | Digest does not resolve cross-platform — verify on target arch |
| `No module named 'tests'` | Add empty `tests/__init__.py` |

## x86 Test Host

```
sambou@192.168.0.210 — Debian 13, Docker 26.1.5, x86_64
Builder: eedom-builder (insecure entitlements enabled)
```

## Before Editing ANY Container Config

1. Read THIS skill first
2. Use context7 MCP for Docker/Podman/uv docs if uncertain
3. Test on x86 host via SSH — not locally on macOS
4. `make test` is the source of truth

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/samfakhreddine/.claude/skills/datum

# DATUM — Agentic Production Line

## Commands

```
/datum go          Run from current phase through merge. Halt at gates.
/datum yolo        Skip optional gates. Hard stops still halt.
/datum <phase>     Run one phase: refine, plan, act, validate, review, closeout, etc.
/datum resume      Resume from .datum/state.json after interruption.
/datum status      Print phase, RUN_ID, lane progress, last failure.
/datum init        Bootstrap repo: hooks, linter, AGENTS.md, CURRENT_STATE.md, ROADMAP.md.
/datum rollback    Revert a merged epic. See references/rollback.md.
/datum classify    Auto-classify epic complexity (Patch/Feature/System)
/datum landscape   Generate docs/LANDSCAPE.md from filesystem analysis
/datum mermaid     Generate Mermaid diagrams — ALWAYS activates on "mermaid", "diagram", "visualize"
/datum dream       Memory consolidation — staleness audit + transcript extraction + pruning
/datum local-llm   Test local MLX inference (beta) — status check or prompt test
```

## Rule: Determinism

Orchestration is deterministic. State, transitions, routing, gates — all enforced by Python scripts. No improvisation. The LLM works within one phase. It does not decide pipeline structure or skip steps. If you are parsing history to figure out where you are, read the state file.

## Dispatcher

Execute in order before any phase work:

**0. Branch Guard** — If on `main`/`master`, auto-create a feature branch and switch. No exceptions. The branch name is descriptive, not generic (#55): slugify the brief/TICKET title into `datum/<slug>` (lowercase ASCII, hyphen-separated, ≤60 chars — `datum.slug.slugify`), de-duplicated against existing branches with a numeric suffix (`datum.slug.make_unique`). Pass the title via `datum state init --title "<title>"` (or `datum init --name "<title>"`); only when no title exists yet does it fall back to `datum/epic-{N}`. Example: "Contact Form: Server-Side Submission" → `datum/contact-form-server-side-submission`, not `datum/epic-8`.

**0.5. Self-check** — `datum doctor`. If it fails, halt.

**1. Load Config** — `.datum/config.toml`, falling back to `assets/config.toml.default`.

**2. Read State** — `datum status --json`. If no state, detect entry:

| Artifact | Entry |
|---|---|
| `docs/epics/$BRANCH/TICKET.md` | Refine |
| `docs/epics/$BRANCH/SPEC.md` (no TASKS.md) | Plan |
| `TASKS.md` + PROPERTIES.md | Act |
| PR URL | PR Comments |
| Nothing | Offer `datum init` |

Epic artifacts always live at `docs/epics/<branch>/`. Never `docs/TICKET.md`.

**2.5. Classify Complexity** — After SPEC.md is detected, run `datum classify`. Routes:

| Tier | Criteria | Pipeline |
|---|---|---|
| Patch | < 50 LOC, ≤ 1 cluster, no new public API | Express (`0x-express.md`) |
| Feature | Standard scope | Standard (full pipeline) |
| System | > 5 clusters, or new subsystem, or multi-package | Extended (units in Plan, all Properties, architect sidecar) |

User can override at `plan_human_approval` gate.

**3. Detect Language** — `datum language-detect`. Maps to `references/04-act-{lang}.md`.

**4. Resolve Tier** — `resolve_tier(phase)` returns `{phase, tier, model}` from config. See `references/model-tiers.md`.

**MANDATORY: Every subagent spawn MUST include an explicit `model:` parameter.** Read `[models.phases]` to get the tier name (e.g., `act_red = "standard"`), then resolve it via `[models]` (e.g., `standard = "claude-sonnet-4-6"`). Map to Agent parameter: `reasoning` → `model: "opus"`, `standard` → `model: "sonnet"`, `fast` → `model: "haiku"`. Never rely on the default model. The config is the authority.

**5. Dispatch Phase** — Load the reference doc, execute it, run the gate.

| Phase | Reference | Gate | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Discovery | `00-discovery.md` | — | |
| Refine | `01-refine.md` | skippable | |
| Plan | `02-plan.md` | **required** | System-tier epics include unit decomposition (step 2.5 in 02-plan.md), grouping tasks into parallelizable units of work. |
| Prior Art | `02.3-prior-art.md` | skippable | Parallel subagents search GitHub, PyPI, internal repos, and the web for existing solutions per task. Can downgrade tasks from "build" to "wrap." |
| Triage | `02.5-triage.md` | **required** | **ALWAYS runs after Prior Art.** Non-skippable, even in Express. |
| Deepen | `02.8-deepen.md` | skipped if triage routes to properties | Triage decides: deepen or skip to properties. |
| Properties | `03-properties.md` | skippable | |
| Architect | `03.5-architect.md` | blocks if ADRs missing | |
| Act | `04-act.md` | per-lane retry ladder | |
| Validate | `05-validate.md` | skippable | |
| Review | `06-review.md` | max 3 iterations | |
| PR Comments | `07-pr-comments.md` | — | |
| Closeout | `08-closeout.md` | — | |

**Sequencing rule:** After Plan gate passes, the next phase is ALWAYS Prior Art, then Triage. Never skip directly to Properties or Act. Prior Art searches for existing solutions per task (can reduce scope). Triage evaluates the plan and routes to Deepen or Properties. This is non-negotiable — skipping Triage in epic-1 caused the pipeline to miss evidence gathering.

After each phase: `datum gate <phase> [--yolo]`

For Act, also load: `agent-contracts.md`, `brief-builder.md`, `04-act-red-brief.md`, `04-act-green-brief.md`, `04-act-refactor-brief.md`, `04-act-adversarial-brief.md`, `04-act-skeleton-preflight.md`, `pipeline-dispatch.md`, `proof-of-work.md`, `spec-drift.md`, `quality-profiles.md`, language override, `gitnexus-playbook.md` (if available).

## Gates

| Gate | Policy | yolo? |
|---|---|---|
| `refine_human_review` | skippable_if_complete | skipped |
| `plan_human_approval` | **required** | **halts** |
| `triage_human_approval` | **required** | **halts** |
| `properties_human_review` | skippable_if_complete | skipped |
| `validate_human_review` | skippable_if_complete | skipped |
| `merge_human_approval` | **required** | **halts** |

> Plan gate also checks: `## Assumption Audit` in SPEC.md (fails if missing or has unresolved guesses). Emits warning if Refine generated zero questions in QUESTIONS.md.

Hard stops never bypass: `tests_red_after_3x_retry`, `hook_blocked_write`, `merge_conflict`, `git_push_rejected`, `schema_validation_failed`, `test_ratchet_violation`, `lane_tool_sandbox_violation`, `external_dependency_install_proposed`.

## Brief Construction

The brief is the agent's entire context. Get it wrong and the contract breaks. Read `references/brief-builder.md`.

- **RED**: task entry, filtered PROPERTIES, GitNexus context, lane-tools README, stub deps. Exclude: test dir, implementation files, other lanes.
- **GREEN**: same as RED + redacted TestSignal JSON. Exclude: test source, test names, RED output.
- **REFACTOR**: everything. Full SPEC, PROPERTIES, tests, implementation, GitNexus impact.

## Artifacts

These artifacts are committed to `docs/epics/<branch>/` and archived to `.datum/runs/<RUN_ID>/`:

| Artifact | Phase | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `TICKET.md` | Input | Original request |
| `SPEC.md` | Refine | Refined requirements + Assumption Audit + Classification Metadata |
| `QUESTIONS.md` | Refine + Plan | Structured Q&A with [Answer]: tags |
| `TASKS.md` | Plan | Implementation plan (root = execution copy, epic dir = archive) |
| `PROPERTIES.md` | Properties | 11-category invariant set |
| `LANDSCAPE.md` | Discovery | Codebase architecture scaffold (project-level, not per-epic) |

## Error Recovery

- `ENVIRONMENTAL` → fix in place, same tier, counter not incremented
- `REASONING` → retry ladder: local (if enabled) → standard → reasoning → reasoning+verbose
- See `references/recovery-modes.md`

**Gemma-First Flow:** When `[local_llm] enabled = true` in config, most phases attempt local MLX inference (Gemma 4 26B) before Claude. The retry ladder: local → standard (Sonnet) → reasoning (Opus). Features:
- **Context monitoring** — checks prompt fits in 128K window before inference
- **Repetition detection** — aborts and escalates if output loops (n-gram detection)
- **Grammar-constrained output** — `datum.local_llm.structured(prompt, Schema)` via outlines forces valid JSON
- **Escalation signal** — model outputs `ESCALATE` or pipeline detects failure → bumps to Claude
- **Metrics** — `datum local-llm --stats` tracks calls, tokens, escalation rate, estimated savings
- Phases routed locally: triage, skeleton, RED, GREEN, REFACTOR, validate, sidecars, closeout collectors

**Self-healing:** On any unexpected error (script crash, missing asset, schema failure on DATUM-generated artifacts), run `datum bugfile <module> "<description>" --trace "<traceback>"` or call `datum.report_bug.report_bug(module, error, context)` from Python. Auto-files a deduplicated GitHub issue with `datum-bug` label. See `AGENTS.md` for the full policy.

## Resume

`datum resume` reads state and continues where it stopped. Completed phases are not re-run. ACT lanes with `in_progress` are re-queued. See `references/recovery-modes.md`.

## Session End

On "session end" or "wrapping up" during a DATUM run, write a handoff to memory:

```
Run ID / Phase / Branch / Lane summary / Decisions / Next action
```

Write to: `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/datum-session-<timestamp>.md`

## Mermaid Diagrams

**Trigger:** Always activates on "mermaid", "diagram", "visualize", "draw the flow", "sequence diagram", "architecture diagram", or `/datum mermaid`.

Built-in diagram and design-doc capability. References and templates are part of the datum package:

| Resource | Use for |
|----------|---------|
| `references/mermaid-diagram-guide.md` | Syntax reference for all diagram types |
| `references/sequence-diagrams.md` | Sequence diagram patterns |
| `references/activity-diagrams.md` | Activity/flowchart patterns |
| `references/architecture-diagrams.md` | C4 and architecture patterns |
| `references/deployment-diagrams.md` | Infrastructure diagrams |
| `references/diagram-legibility.md` | High-contrast styling rules |
| `references/unicode-symbols.md` | Semantic unicode for diagram labels |
| `references/troubleshooting.md` | Mermaid syntax error fixes |
| `references/resilient-workflow.md` | Validate-before-embed workflow |

**Templates:** `templates/system-design-template.md`, `templates/architecture-design-template.md`, `templates/api-design-template.md`, `templates/feature-design-template.md`, `templates/database-design-template.md`

**Scripts:** `scripts/resilient_diagram.py` (validate), `scripts/mermaid_to_image.py` (render PNG), `scripts/extract_mermaid.py` (extract from markdown)

**Rules:**
1. NEVER embed a diagram without validating it first via `datum mermaid validate`
2. ALWAYS use high-contrast styling and unicode semantic symbols
3. PREFER design templates from `templates/` when creating design documents

## Cross-Tool

SKILL.md is tool-agnostic. Subagent primitives are in `assets/config.toml.default` under `[tools]`. Model tiers resolve per-tool via `[models]`. See `references/model-tiers.md`.

7	/// A single versioned, named schema migration step.
8	public struct MigrationStep: Sendable {
9	    /// Human-readable name for logging and diagnostics.
10	    public let name: String
11	
12	    /// The schema version the database must be at before this step can run.
13	    public let fromVersion: Int32

20	    public let migrate: @Sendable (Connection) throws -> Void
21	
22	    public init(
23	        name: String,
24	        fromVersion: Int32,
25	        toVersion: Int32,
26	        migrate: @escaping @Sendable (Connection) throws -> Void
27	    ) {

35	// MARK: - DuckDBMigrationRunner
36	
37	/// Executes versioned, ordered, idempotent schema migrations against a DuckDB connection.
38	///
39	/// Schema version is tracked via `PRAGMA user_version` (an integer stored in the DuckDB file header).
40	/// On each `migrate(connection:)` call, only steps whose `fromVersion` matches the current version
41	/// are applied — already-applied steps are skipped.
42	///
43	/// Each step is wrapped in a BEGIN/ROLLBACK transaction. If a step throws, the transaction is
44	/// rolled back and `StorageError.migrationFailed` is thrown — leaving `user_version` unchanged.
45	public final class DuckDBMigrationRunner: Sendable {
46	
47	    // MARK: - Public state
48	
49	    /// Ordered list of migration steps this runner will apply.
50	    public let steps: [MigrationStep]
51	
52	    /// The schema version that a fully-migrated database should be at.
53	    public var currentSchemaVersion: Int32 {
54	        steps.last?.toVersion ?? 0
55	    }
56	
57	    /// Versions applied during the most recent `migrate(connection:)` call (ascending order).
58	    /// Protected by the serial nature of `migrate` — callers must `await` before reading.
59	    public nonisolated(unsafe) private(set) var appliedVersions: [Int32] = []
60	
61	    // MARK: - Init
62	
63	    /// Creates a runner with an explicit set of steps (primarily for testing).
64	    public init(steps: [MigrationStep]) {
65	        self.steps = steps
66	    }
67	
68	    /// Creates a runner with the production migration plan.
69	    public convenience init() {
70	        self.init(steps: DuckDBMigrationRunner.productionSteps)
71	    }
72	
73	    // MARK: - migrate
74	
75	    /// Applies all pending migrations to `connection` in ascending version order.
76	    ///
77	    /// Each step is wrapped in an explicit transaction. On failure the transaction is rolled
78	    /// back and `StorageError.migrationFailed` is thrown. The `user_version` pragma is updated
79	    /// inside the same transaction so it stays in sync.
80	    ///
81	    /// Calling `migrate` again after a successful run is a no-op.
82	    public func migrate(connection: Connection) async throws {
83	        var applied: [Int32] = []
84	
85	        for step in steps {
86	            let currentVersion = try readUserVersion(connection: connection)
87	
88	            // Skip steps that have already been applied.
89	            guard currentVersion == step.fromVersion else {
90	                continue
91	            }
92	
93	            // Each step runs inside a transaction so partial DDL can be rolled back.
94	            do {
95	                try connection.execute("BEGIN TRANSACTION")
96	                try step.migrate(connection)
97	                try connection.execute("PRAGMA user_version = \(step.toVersion)")
98	                try connection.execute("COMMIT")
99	                applied.append(step.toVersion)
100	            } catch {
101	                // Roll back the partial work and re-throw as a StorageError.
102	                try? connection.execute("ROLLBACK")
103	                throw StorageError.migrationFailed(underlying: AnyError(error))
104	            }
105	        }
106	
107	        appliedVersions = applied
108	    }
109	
110	    // MARK: - Helpers
111	
112	    private func readUserVersion(connection: Connection) throws -> Int32 {
113	        let result = try connection.query("PRAGMA user_version")
114	        let col = result[0].cast(to: Int32.self)
115	        return col[0] ?? 0
116	    }
117	}

```sql

Add a new column with name `k` to the table `integers`, it will be filled with the default value `NULL`:

Add a new column with name `l` to the table integers, it will be filled with the default value 10:

ALTER TABLE integers

Drop the column `k` from the table integers:

```sql
ALTER TABLE integers

Change the type of the column `i` to the type `VARCHAR` using a standard cast:

```sql
ALTER TABLE integers
ALTER i TYPE VARCHAR;
```

Change the type of the column `i` to the type `VARCHAR`, using the specified expression to convert the data for each row:

```sql
ALTER TABLE integers
ALTER i SET DATA TYPE VARCHAR USING concat(i, '_', j);
```

Set the default value of a column:

```sql
ALTER TABLE integers
ALTER COLUMN i SET DEFAULT 10;
```

Drop the default value of a column:

```sql
ALTER TABLE integers
ALTER COLUMN i DROP DEFAULT;

Make a column not nullable:

ALTER TABLE integers

Drop the not-`NULL` constraint:

```sql
ALTER TABLE integers
ALTER COLUMN i DROP NOT NULL;
```

Rename a table:

```sql
ALTER TABLE integers
RENAME TO integers_old;
```

Rename a column of a table:

```sql

RENAME i TO ii;

Add a primary key to a column of a table:

```sql

Change the type of the column `i` to the type `VARCHAR` using a standard cast:

```sql
ALTER TABLE integers
ALTER i TYPE VARCHAR;
```

> Instead of
> `ALTER ⟨column_name⟩ TYPE ⟨type⟩`{:.language-sql .highlight}, you can also use the equivalent
> `ALTER ⟨column_name⟩ SET TYPE ⟨type⟩`{:.language-sql .highlight} and the 
> `ALTER ⟨column_name⟩ SET DATA TYPE ⟨type⟩`{:.language-sql .highlight} clauses.

Change the type of the column `i` to the type `VARCHAR`, using the specified expression to convert the data for each row:

```sql
ALTER TABLE integers
ALTER i SET DATA TYPE VARCHAR USING concat(i, '_', j);
```

The `[SET [DATA]] TYPE` clause changes the type of a column in a table. Any data present in the column is converted according to the provided expression in the `USING` clause, or, if the `USING` clause is absent, cast to the new data type. Note that columns can only have their type changed if they do not have any indexes that rely on them and are not part of any `CHECK` constraints.

### Handling Structs

There are two options to change the sub-schema of a [`STRUCT`]({% link docs/lts/sql/data_types/struct.md %})-typed column.

#### `ALTER TABLE` with `struct_insert`

You can use `ALTER TABLE` with the `struct_insert` function.
For example:

```sql
CREATE TABLE tbl (col STRUCT(i INTEGER));
ALTER TABLE tbl
ALTER col TYPE USING struct_insert(col, a := 42, b := NULL::VARCHAR);
```

#### `ALTER TABLE` with `ADD COLUMN` / `DROP COLUMN` / `RENAME COLUMN`

Starting with DuckDB v1.3.0, `ALTER TABLE` supports the
[`ADD COLUMN`, `DROP COLUMN` and `RENAME COLUMN` clauses]({% link docs/lts/sql/data_types/struct.md %}#updating-the-schema)
to update the sub-schema of a `STRUCT`.","score":7.784949076621913}]
